week.worked: The armband. B.Fernandes scored three at Old Trafford, Mbeumo got the fifth, and João Pedro and Rogers both returned at Stamford Bridge. Your best week of the season, and you spent neither a transfer nor a chip on it.
week.didnt: The back four. Kerkez has one point from two full games, Shaw had the worst afternoon of any United player in a five-goal win, and Verbruggen let in four. Calafiori is the only defender you own with a game left to play.

watchlist.name: Gvardiol
watchlist.note: Kerkez was taken off on 71 minutes and has one point in two games. Gvardiol costs a tenth of a million more and has started every week whatever back line City pick.

watchlist.name: Palmer
watchlist.note: You own two Chelsea attackers and not the one who scored the winner on Sunday. He takes the penalties and the price has moved twice already.

big.call: Dubravka, a £4.0m keeper who cannot play
big.why: Kinsky starts every week at Spurs, so your second goalkeeper is a slot rather than a player. Your free transfer has been banked since day one and the window shuts on Tuesday night.

big.call: Kerkez or Gvardiol, at about the same money
big.why: Kerkez was replaced on 71 minutes at home and Liverpool have conceded four in two games. Gvardiol has kept his shirt through every shape Maresca has tried, and City are at home to Coventry in GW3.

week.worked: The Bench Boost, in a week nobody would have chosen for one. Lammens kept United in the first half, Schade scored at Elland Road, Calvert-Lewin equalised against him, Groß headed one in at the 96th minute, and B.Fernandes captained the lot. You lead the five.
week.didnt: Your two £4.0m Coventry defenders. Coventry lost at home to Hull, have no points and no goals, and go to the Etihad next. On the one week your bench actually counted, they were the part that didn't.

watchlist.name: Ajayi
watchlist.note: Same price as your Coventry pair. Hull have won both games and kept both clean sheets, and one of those wins was at Coventry.

watchlist.name: Ødegaard
watchlist.note: You own an Arsenal defender and no Arsenal attacker. Three weeks of the brain saying so and nobody in the room has fixed it.

big.call: Your Coventry defenders, and City at the Etihad
big.why: Coventry have lost both games and scored nothing, and GW3 is away at City. The Bench Boost is spent now, so those two have stopped being a squad and gone back to being a bench.

big.call: The armband, with United away at Everton
big.why: B.Fernandes has worn it two weeks running and has just scored three. GW3 is Everton away, GW4 is City at Old Trafford, so the question is whether it ever leaves him or only leaves him in the wrong week.

week.worked: The mid-price spine again. Gvardiol started at left-back, Rogers made a goal at Stamford Bridge, Szoboszlai and Ndiaye both returned, and B.Fernandes went on top of them. No chip spent, no transfer made, third of the five.
week.didnt: Twelve points on your bench for the second week running. Calvert-Lewin scored Leeds' equaliser while sitting on it, and your goalkeeper slot is still at the club that is bottom of the table with no goals.

watchlist.name: Cherki
watchlist.note: You own Gvardiol, so you have watched this side up close. Cherki costs about what Rogers does and has the most points of any midfielder in the game.

watchlist.name: Tarkowski
watchlist.note: You own the Everton midfielder who may not be an Everton player by Wednesday. Tarkowski is the same club bought from the end nobody is bidding for.

big.call: Ndiaye, with the window shutting Tuesday
big.why: Spurs are in advanced talks, the clubs have largely agreed a deal, and City have asked too. He is a £6.0m midfielder who could be in a different shirt three days before Friday's deadline.

big.call: Calvert-Lewin on your bench, two weeks running
big.why: He scored Leeds' equaliser on Sunday from behind your eleven, and twelve points have now gone begging twice. The problem is the bench order rather than the fifteen names.

week.worked: João Pedro repaid the armband at Stamford Bridge, Maguire scored at Old Trafford, and Mbeumo got United's fifth. Three returns from three different games, in a week that gave you very little else.
week.didnt: You are the only gaffer in the room without B.Fernandes, on the afternoon he scored three. Aït-Nouri and Greaves are still slots rather than players, Kinsky is at the bottom club, and Semenyo has one assist all season at £8.5m.

watchlist.name: Cherki
watchlist.note: You pay £8.5m for Semenyo on City's left. Cherki is a million cheaper, plays in the same team, and has three times the points.

watchlist.name: Elanga
watchlist.note: He scored at Spurs and Newcastle have the kindest six-game run on the ticker. You own nobody there, and Jaissle is still trying to buy another forward.

big.call: Two bench slots that are not players
big.why: Aït-Nouri has not been in a City matchday squad and Greaves is a £4.0m Ipswich defender. You are last of the five with £0.9m in the bank, and two of your fifteen have never been picked to play.
Semenyo has one assist all season and he is the most expensive midfielder you own. Cherki is in the same team, a million cheaper, and City are at home to Coventry on Saturday.

week.worked: B.Fernandes captained on hat-trick day, with Maguire scoring at the other end of the same game. Rogers, Szoboszlai, Ndiaye, João Pedro and Calvert-Lewin all returned as well, and you held second without touching the squad.
week.didnt: Fifteen points sat on your bench, the biggest in the room. Cash is on minus one for the season, and your week is not even finished — Cash and Konsa both play tonight, while Sir Fergie banked his on Sunday and went thirty-one clear.

watchlist.name: Gvardiol
watchlist.note: Your defence is Calafiori, Cash, Maguire, Konsa and Diop, and three of those clubs spent the weekend selling. Gvardiol is the one City defender whose job has not moved.

watchlist.name: Tarkowski
watchlist.note: You own Ndiaye, who may be a Spurs player by Tuesday night. Tarkowski captains the same club and nobody has bid for him.

big.call: Ndiaye, with the window shutting Tuesday
big.why: Spurs are in advanced talks with Everton, the clubs have largely agreed a deal, and City have also asked. You are second by thirty-one and one of your midfielders may change club before Friday.

big.call: Cash at Villa and Konsa at Arsenal, both tonight
big.why: Villa have now sold Watkins, Martinez and Konsa himself, and Cash is on minus one point. Konsa sits on your bench at a club missing Saliba and Timber. One game answers both before the window shuts.

watchlist.name: Cherki
watchlist.note: The most points of any midfielder in the game, and not one of the five owns him. The trigger was a start. He got it, scored twice, and ownership has climbed every day since.

watchlist.name: Palmer
watchlist.note: Still the miss of the season. Thirteen on the opening night, the winner against Brighton, the penalties, and a Chelsea side built around him while all five watched.

watchlist.name: Ajayi
watchlist.note: Hull have won both and conceded nothing, and they defend on purpose — 182 passes at Coventry against Coventry's 501. This is the cheapest defender price in the game.

watchlist.name: Tarkowski
watchlist.note: Everton's captain, on set pieces, at a club whose two saleable names are both mid-move. He is the one nobody has bid for.

watchlist.name: Elanga
watchlist.note: Scored at Spurs, and Newcastle have the kindest six-game run on the ticker. Nobody in the room owns a Newcastle player, and Jaissle wants one more forward before Tuesday.

watchlist.name: Ødegaard
watchlist.note: Four of the five own an Arsenal defender. None owns the Arsenal player who has outscored them, at £6.6m, with Chelsea visiting in GW3.

verdicts.name: B.Fernandes
verdicts.why: The trigger was a blank at home to Ipswich. He scored a hat-trick instead, including a penalty after missing two in pre-season, and four of the five had the armband on him.
verdicts.trigger: Two quiet weeks with United losing, or the contract talk turning into a January move. At £12.0m the price only works while he is the whole team.

verdicts.name: Mbeumo
verdicts.why: Held his wide position, threatened all afternoon and got the fifth goal at the end. First return since the opening weekend.
verdicts.trigger: Rashford keeping the left and United's returns concentrating there instead. Two blanks with Rashford scoring and £8.0m is the wrong United winger.

verdicts.name: Shaw
verdicts.why: A difficult day against Fatawu in a game United won 5-2 — the one home player who struggled. United's deadline plan still has a left-back in it if Zirkzee leaves.
verdicts.trigger: Tuesday at 23:00. A left-back arriving ends a £4.5m pick whose entire case is that he never misses.

verdicts.name: Maguire
verdicts.why: Scored, albeit off a deflection the Ipswich manager thinks should have been ruled out for handball, and was the reliable one in the middle of a defence that could have buckled.
verdicts.trigger: Losing his place when United's other centre-backs are fit. The goal is a bonus; the seat is the asset.

verdicts.name: Lammens
verdicts.why: Kept United in the game with first-half saves, read the Enciso one-on-one perfectly, and was picked out as the calming influence in a panicked defence.
verdicts.trigger: Two more weeks conceding twice. A £5.0m goalkeeper who saves but never keeps a clean sheet is a floor, not an asset.

verdicts.name: Rashford
verdicts.why: First league start for United since December 2024, ran at Ipswich all afternoon and nearly made one for Mbeumo. Now the club's highest earner at £7.0m and 1.6% ownership.
verdicts.trigger: A second start and a return. One game back from two years out is a team sheet, not a player.

verdicts.name: Palmer
verdicts.why: Curled in the 75th-minute winner against Brighton after pressing all afternoon, and Chelsea have now won both league games with him at the centre of them.
verdicts.trigger: Two games spent wide rather than at ten, or the calf flag returning.

verdicts.name: João Pedro
verdicts.why: A flick for the first, the finish for the third, and an own goal in between — messy, but he is the reference point in Chelsea's attack and 69% of the game owns him.
verdicts.trigger: Two Chelsea games without a shot in the box. At that ownership he becomes the risk rather than the floor.

verdicts.name: Rogers
verdicts.why: His running down the flank made Chelsea's second, and he should have had another assist. Three starts from three since the £117m move.
verdicts.trigger: A week wide right or on the bench once Chelsea's midfield is whole. Caicedo going off in tears makes that less likely, not more.

verdicts.name: Martinez
verdicts.why: Thrown straight in after one training session, claimed his crosses and was blamed for none of the three. Alonso: "we will feel his presence".
verdicts.trigger: Chelsea have gone 18 games without a clean sheet, their longest run since the 1960s. Until that breaks, this is a goalkeeper buying save points.

verdicts.name: Lacroix
verdicts.why: The trigger was a clean sheet against a Brighton side missing four forwards. Chelsea conceded three, he was confident on the ball and ragged out of it, and Arsenal are next.
verdicts.trigger: Settled. A £6.0m defender in a back three that has conceded five in two weeks is not a defender.

verdicts.name: Caicedo
verdicts.why: Came on as a substitute and left the pitch in tears after eleven minutes. Whatever the diagnosis, it is not a fortnight.
verdicts.trigger: Settled by the injury. Revisit when he starts a league game.

verdicts.name: Enzo
verdicts.why: Missed the Brighton win with his exile in a second match, and City are expected to bid more than £120m before Tuesday.
verdicts.trigger: The deadline passing with him at Chelsea and back in central midfield. That is not the way to bet.

verdicts.name: Neto
verdicts.why: Tapped in Chelsea's second and put a chance on a plate for João Pedro, but was most at fault in the build-up to Brighton's first and is still linked with a move.
verdicts.trigger: Tuesday night with him still at Chelsea, plus one more start. At 1.2% ownership a starting Chelsea forward is a real differential.

verdicts.name: Welbeck
verdicts.why: The trigger was a league start. He was an unused substitute against Brighton with Chelsea three goals up and then hanging on.
verdicts.trigger: Settled by the team sheet. A forward who cannot get on at 4-3 is not a £5.9m pick.

verdicts.name: Verbruggen
verdicts.why: Struggled to claim the ball for Chelsea's opener and let in four, though he made several good saves after it. Owned by three of the five.
verdicts.trigger: Leeds at home in GW3. A £4.5m goalkeeper is bought for clean sheets and Brighton have kept one in two.

verdicts.name: De Cuyper
verdicts.why: The trigger was a second attacking return with Brighton's forward line unavailable. Instead the injuries pushed him into an unfamiliar advanced role and he offered nothing in it.
verdicts.trigger: A return to left-back and a clean sheet. £4.6m for a makeshift winger is the wrong purchase at the wrong position.

verdicts.name: Groß
verdicts.why: Crossed for Brighton's first and headed in a 96th-minute consolation, on penalties at £5.5m. Three of the five own him and all three had him on the bench.
verdicts.trigger: A start in the room's elevens, or two weeks without a return. At 33 the minutes are the question, not the quality.

verdicts.name: Calafiori
verdicts.why: Owned by four of the five and 41.6% of the game, at £5.6m, and he has not played his gameweek yet.
verdicts.trigger: The knee trouble that has followed him around, or Arsenal's Champions League calendar producing genuine rotation.

verdicts.name: Ødegaard
verdicts.why: A fortnight later and still nobody in the room owns him at £6.6m, which stopped being an oversight some time around Thursday.
verdicts.trigger: A repeat of last season's injury record, or Arsenal's returns concentrating in Saka and Gyökeres instead.

verdicts.name: Saka
verdicts.why: Arsenal's penalties at £9.5m with barely 10% of the game on him, and a Villa side that has sold three first-teamers waiting tonight.
verdicts.trigger: The recurring hamstring, or rotation once the European nights start.

verdicts.name: Konsa
verdicts.why: A £4.4m defender expected to debut at the club he spent seven seasons at, in an Arsenal defence missing both first-choice centre-backs.
verdicts.trigger: Named in the eleven tonight and this is the cheapest starting defender at the champions. Left out and only the price recommends him.

verdicts.name: Mosquera
verdicts.why: Six points deputising while Saliba and Timber are both out with no return date. The points are real and the seat is borrowed.
verdicts.trigger: Konsa starting tonight. That is this pick ending rather than threatening to.

verdicts.name: Havertz
verdicts.why: Arsenal are still in the market for Julián Álvarez at a fee near £128m, which is a striker signed over the top of him rather than alongside him.
verdicts.trigger: Tuesday night with no forward arriving. Then £7.5m at 7% ownership is a fair price for the man who starts.

verdicts.name: Tzolis
verdicts.why: 26% of the game is on him after one debut and the price has not moved. Two of the five own him and he has not played his gameweek yet.
verdicts.trigger: Saka and Rice fully fit squeezing the minutes.

verdicts.name: Szoboszlai
verdicts.why: On the penalties at £7.0m and owned by three of the five, in a Liverpool side that has drawn twice and needs him to keep the midfield honest.
verdicts.trigger: A shift to right-back, which Iraola has an obvious hole at. That halves the appeal without changing the price.

verdicts.name: Kerkez
verdicts.why: The trigger was one start missed. He was replaced on 71 minutes at Anfield instead, which is the same evidence arriving a week early, and Liverpool have conceded four in two.
verdicts.trigger: Settled unless he goes 90 minutes twice with a clean sheet. £5.5m for a full-back who does not attack is the wrong end of the market.

verdicts.name: Gakpo
verdicts.why: City have opened talks at around £85m, City is his preferred destination, and Liverpool will sanction it if one more attacker arrives on top of Barcola.
verdicts.trigger: Tuesday night passing with him at Liverpool. Then seventeen points at £7.0m is the cheapest returning Liverpool attacker.

verdicts.name: Haaland
verdicts.why: Two at Selhurst Park, owned by all five and 69% of the game, and Coventry come to the Etihad on Saturday having lost both and scored nothing.
verdicts.trigger: A serious injury, or three weeks of City creating through Cherki and Foden and past him.

verdicts.name: Cherki
verdicts.why: The most points of any midfielder in the game, at £7.6m, and still owned by none of the five in the second week of the brain saying so.
verdicts.trigger: Doku back and Maresca deciding the free role costs too much off the ball. Until then this is the room's clearest miss.

verdicts.name: Gvardiol
verdicts.why: Started at left-back again and inverted into midfield inside the 4-1-4-1. He is still the only City defender you can name in advance.
verdicts.trigger: O'Reilly reclaiming the left side once Doku is back on 5 September.

verdicts.name: Semenyo
verdicts.why: One assist all season at £8.5m, and the two City attackers either side of him cost less and score more.
verdicts.trigger: A goal against Coventry at home. If it does not come in that fixture, £8.5m is a sack.

verdicts.name: Aït-Nouri
verdicts.why: Still no points, still 0.7% ownership, still behind O'Reilly and Gvardiol, and still occupying a bench slot for the gaffer at the bottom of the five.
verdicts.trigger: A start. Until then this is a squad place doing no work at all.

verdicts.name: Calvert-Lewin
verdicts.why: Scored Leeds' equaliser after Farke switched to a back four, which is what a £6.0m forward owned by four of the five is bought to do.
verdicts.trigger: Losing the penalties, or Leeds signing an attacker before Tuesday and changing the shape around him.

verdicts.name: Trafford
verdicts.why: The trigger was a third clean sheet against Brentford. Leeds conceded once and drew, so it is not settled either way, and he is still £5.0m at 4.9%.
verdicts.trigger: Two clean sheets in the next three. The cheap goalkeeper bracket is where the value is this season and Hull have the better one.

verdicts.name: Ndiaye
verdicts.why: Spurs are in advanced talks, the clubs have largely agreed, and City have asked too. Owned by two of the five at £6.0m with three days to go.
verdicts.trigger: Tuesday night at Everton and this stays a solid. A move to Spurs makes him a squad player at a club that has not scored in two games.

verdicts.name: Tarkowski
verdicts.why: Everton's captain, on set pieces, scoring the late equaliser his trigger asked for — and the only saleable name at the club nobody has bid for.
verdicts.trigger: Two games without a header or a clean sheet, and this is a set-piece bet rather than a defender.

verdicts.name: Barry
verdicts.why: Everton's first-choice striker at £5.5m and 3.9% ownership, and Richarlison arriving would be competition for exactly that shirt.
verdicts.trigger: Richarlison signing. That is this pick ending, and it may happen before Friday's deadline.

verdicts.name: Elanga
verdicts.why: Opened the scoring at Spurs and has been described as revitalised under Jaissle. Seventeen points at £6.1m and 5% ownership, in front of the kindest six-game run on the ticker.
verdicts.trigger: Fernandez-Pardo arriving from Lille, where he has been left out of training until the window shuts. That is a winger bought for his flank.

verdicts.name: Wissa
verdicts.why: Led the line with what the reporting called ferocious energy and scored at Spurs, at the same price as the Newcastle forward two of these pages preferred.
verdicts.trigger: One week out of the side once another forward arrives. At £6.1m the case is the shirt.

verdicts.name: Woltemade
verdicts.why: The trigger was a league start ahead of Wissa. He got an assist off the bench instead, was described as maligned in the same sentence, and Napoli have asked about a loan.
verdicts.trigger: Settled. Same price, same club, and the other one is playing.

verdicts.name: Kinsky
verdicts.why: Owned by three of the five at a club that is bottom, has not scored in two games, and had three players ask to leave in the same week.
verdicts.trigger: Reassess at GW7 — window shut, players settled, fixtures softer. Until then this is a bench goalkeeper.

verdicts.name: Hume
verdicts.why: Sunderland kept their first clean sheet of the season with Mukiele outstanding in the middle of it, which is good for the £4.5m defenders around him.
verdicts.trigger: A second week pushed forward into the wing role. A defender who does not defend is priced wrong for the position.

verdicts.name: E.Le Fée
verdicts.why: Sunderland won without him producing anything, and at £5.9m the case was always that the side plays through him.
verdicts.trigger: A return in the next two, or the money goes to a midfielder who takes shots.

verdicts.name: Ajer
verdicts.why: Kept his place and Brentford took a point at Elland Road, but the club has bought five players including a £40m left-back and a centre-back.
verdicts.trigger: One rotation. A £4.5m centre-back at a club buying defenders holds his seat on loan.

verdicts.name: Schade
verdicts.why: Scored the opener at Elland Road at £6.0m and 3.6% ownership, and he is the Brentford attacker whose place has not been bought over.
verdicts.trigger: Thiago rediscovering the shirt, or two blanks in a side that has drawn twice.

verdicts.name: Ajayi
verdicts.why: Dominated the middle of a Hull defence that has now kept two clean sheets from two, at the cheapest defender price in the game and 4.8% ownership.
verdicts.trigger: Villa at home this week is the honest test. A goal conceded there does not end it; a week out of the back four does.

verdicts.name: Mendy
verdicts.why: Sixteen points at £4.0m in the same defence, but he threw his hands up and pulled his shirt over his head when he was taken off on the hour at Coventry.
verdicts.trigger: Hull have made thirteen signings and want another right-back before Tuesday. One rotation and a £4.0m defender is a bench place.

verdicts.name: Tzolakis
verdicts.why: Twenty points from two clean sheets at £4.5m, behind a side that gives the ball away on purpose and defends the box for ninety minutes.
verdicts.trigger: Jakirovic wants another goalkeeper before Tuesday. That is the only thing that ends this.

verdicts.name: Cash
verdicts.why: Villa have now sold Watkins, Konsa and Martinez, their manager says Chelsea "want to kill us", and Arsenal arrive at Villa Park tonight.
verdicts.trigger: Two clean sheets in three once the window is shut. Nothing before Wednesday counts.

signals.text: Came on as a substitute against Brighton and "his afternoon was cut short after just 11 minutes as he left the pitch in tears". Chelsea had already had concerns over his fitness before kick-off.
signals.action: the Chelsea midfield is being picked by absences again. Rogers and Palmer keep their minutes; nobody should buy Caicedo

signals.text: Hat-trick in the 5-2 comeback against Ipswich, including a penalty taken after two pre-season misses. Carrick: "Times like today, when you're looking towards certain players to give us that little bit of something else, he did particularly well."
signals.action: the trigger written on Monday was a blank at home to Ipswich. It fired the other way, so £12.0m stays

signals.text: "A difficult day for the England full-back. Struggled to deal with Fatawu." Rated the lowest of United's back line in a game they won 5-2.
signals.action: United's deadline plan still has a left-back in it if Zirkzee leaves. Two of the five hold Shaw at £4.5m

signals.text: Scored via a deflection that the Ipswich manager called a "blatant" handball, with the goal allowed to stand. "Reliable presence at the heart of the home defence, then got lucky with the deflection."
signals.action: a £5.0m defender who scores is a bonus. Two of the five own him and the seat is the actual asset

signals.text: "The goalkeeper produced some important first-half saves against Ipswich to keep his side in the game in difficult circumstances... a calming influence in an emotional environment, especially with a panicked defence."
signals.action: the trigger was clean sheets or enough saves to justify the floor. He has produced the saves, not the clean sheets

signals.text: "Tottenham are in advanced talks to sign Iliman Ndiaye from Everton, with Richarlison set to move in the opposite direction... Although a deal is largely agreed between the two clubs, it remains unclear whether he will make the switch, with Manchester City among the clubs to have expressed an interest."
signals.action: two of the five own him at £6.0m. Nothing about him is settled before Tuesday night

signals.text: Missed the Brighton win as his exile from the first team entered a second match, with City expected to bid before Tuesday's deadline in a deal worth more than £120m.
signals.action: settled in all but the paperwork. Chelsea are already shopping for Camara to replace him

signals.text: "City are willing to offer a deal worth around £85m and sources indicate that City is Gakpo's preferred destination." Liverpool will only sanction it if one more attacker arrives on top of Barcola.
signals.action: seventeen points at £7.0m and three days to find out which shirt he is in on Friday

signals.text: "Offered little attacking threat while operating in an unfamiliar advanced role because of Brighton's injury problems." Rated among the lowest of the Brighton side in a 4-3 defeat.
signals.action: his seventeen points came from attacking returns at left-back. He is not playing left-back

signals.text: Crossed for Brighton's first goal and headed in a consolation in the 96th minute at Stamford Bridge, after a long throw was not dealt with.
signals.action: three of the five own him and all three had him on the bench. Only the Bench Boost collected

signals.text: Scored the equaliser against Brentford after Farke switched from a back five to a back four at half-time — "a much better second-half showing, a deserved equaliser and a point Leeds were good value for".
signals.action: four of the five own him and one of them had him on the bench. That is the second week running

signals.text: Scored the 75th-minute winner with a curling finish, having pressed well and missed a good chance earlier. Chelsea have won both league games under Alonso.
signals.action: nobody in the room owns him and the price has risen twice. This is the miss of the season so far

signals.text: Chelsea have gone 18 games without a clean sheet, their longest run since the 1960s. They had 25.9% possession and completed 146 passes against Brighton, both club records in the Premier League, and Alonso has switched to a back three.
signals.action: no Chelsea defender or goalkeeper is a clean-sheet buy, and Arsenal away in GW3 is the worst week to find out otherwise

signals.text: The £40m Armstrong sale to Forest was called off after a fan revolt, Ndiaye is in advanced talks with Spurs, Richarlison has agreed terms to return, a Grealish loan is close and Everton are chasing Tete at right-back.
signals.action: the two Everton assets the room cares about are on opposite sides of this. Nothing here is settled before Wednesday, so hold rather than buy

signals.text: Barcola is arriving for £123m, but Iraola still has holes at right-wing, right-back and central midfield, and Liverpool have drawn 2-2 twice. "We don't know what the squad is going to be on 2 September."
signals.action: Liverpool defenders are not clean-sheet buys yet. Ipswich away in GW3 is the softest test they will get to prove otherwise

signals.text: Two wins, two clean sheets, and 182 passes at Coventry to Coventry's 501. "We prefer letting the other team have the ball and just defending." Jakirovic wants a right-back and another goalkeeper before Tuesday.
signals.action: the £4.0m defenders and the £4.5m goalkeeper are a real buy, not a haul. Check the team sheet on Friday for the new right-back

signals.text: United's remaining deadline business centres on moving Zirkzee out, and "Zirkzee's exit might open the door for a left-back or a reinforcement in the forward department, although that too might initially be a loan".
signals.action: Shaw at £4.5m is the pick that hangs on Tuesday night. Everton away in GW3, City at home in GW4

signals.text: Richarlison, Danso and Sarr have all asked to leave and none were in the squad for the home defeat by Newcastle. Spurs are bottom with no goals in two games after spending more than £300m.
signals.action: three of the five own the Spurs goalkeeper and one owns the reserve as well. There is still no reason to start either

signals.text: Jaissle built the win at Spurs from players written off after poor seasons — Wissa, Elanga and Willock — with Nico González impressing on debut. He is still pushing for Lille's Fernandez-Pardo, who has been excluded from training until the window shuts.
signals.action: buy the Newcastle wide players now rather than after Tuesday. Nobody in the room owns one and the fixtures are the best on the ticker

doctrine.text: Rank insurance is a real cost — price the drift on every call.
New-manager minutes are unknowable until three XIs.
Champions' template assets are default-own; passing needs a priced case.
Opening weekend prices nothing. A promoted side beating a giant is one result until the same shape holds twice — sell on a pattern, never on a scoreline.
A cheap-defender haul is a match, not a seat. Before buying points that already happened, check the player is still fit and still first choice.

Grade a chip against its own median week — and then check the table before saying it did not matter. Six points from a Bench Boost is a chip spent rather than used; it is also, exactly, the six points between first of the five and second.

Buy the line-up, not the scoreboard. Three of the weekend’s best mid-price returns came from players who started on a bench or out of position, and two of the room’s bench slots are held by players who have not been in a matchday eleven.

A player the whole room passed on is a bigger exposure than a player the whole room owns. All five owned Haaland and João Pedro; none owned Palmer, who outscored both. Check the consensus blind spot before checking the consensus pick.
An open window is a team-sheet risk, not a shopping opportunity. Buy after the window shuts, not into it.

A cup tie is a team sheet, not a fixture. The goals are worth nothing and the selection is worth everything — which is why a 35-year-old’s header, a flagged striker’s replacement and a vice-captain’s absence were the three things worth reading on Thursday night.

Write triggers a transfer can settle, not only ones that need ninety minutes. Two calls were resolved this week without a ball being kicked: the Chelsea goalkeeper, because Chelsea signed one, and the Liverpool winger, because Liverpool bought over him. A trigger that only a scoreline can fire will sit open through the weeks that actually decide the player.

A room that agrees has no insurance. Not one of the five captained Haaland this week — the three who did in GW1 all moved off him — and he scored twice at Palace before any of their captains had kicked a ball. Check what the room has quietly agreed on, not only what it argues about.

Grade a rule by what it cost, not by how sensible it sounded. D5 declined the £4.0m Hull defenders after one haul because they were flagged and it was one match. Two weeks on Hull have six points, two clean sheets, and the two best-scoring £4.0m defenders in the game. A rule that only ever says no is not a rule, it is a mood.

A Bench Boost wants fifteen players who start, not a double gameweek. The page called Sir Fergie's chip premature on Saturday, and by Sunday night every one of his fifteen had played and it had won him the week and the lead. Grade a chip on the team sheet it lands on, not on the calendar.

roast.text: The Special One was the only gaffer in the room without B.Fernandes, on the afternoon United's captain scored three at Old Trafford. The other four spent Sunday watching the same man; he spent it being the only one with an independent opinion.

plan.outlook: Nineteen of Gameweek 2's twenty fixtures are done and the room has been rearranged. Sir Fergie played a Bench Boost in an ordinary week, watched all fifteen of his players turn up, and went thirty-one clear at the top of the five. Four of the others captained the same man and got a hat-trick for it, so the week separated nobody except The Special One, who did not own him and is now last. One game is left: Arsenal at Villa Park tonight, which finishes the week for Le Professeur, who still has Cash and Konsa in it, and for the four who hold Calafiori. Then the real work. The window shuts on Tuesday at 23:00 and the GW3 deadline is Friday at 23:00, so for the first time this season a transfer can be made with the team sheets known rather than guessed. Ndiaye is the one to have an answer ready for — two of the five own him and Spurs have largely agreed a deal. Cherki and Palmer are the two nobody owns and both keep scoring.

chips.note: First-half chips die at the GW19 deadline (2 Jan). Both of the room's chips so far have been played outside a double gameweek. Le Professeur's returned six points in GW1 and was graded here as spent rather than used; Sir Fergie's returned the best week anyone has had and the lead. The difference was not the calendar, it was that all fifteen of his players started. The next honest chip conversation is GW6–8: window shut a fortnight, three settled line-ups and a fixture run you can read.

log.call: Day-0 squad: Haaland (C) vs BOU; bets on Palmer, Kerkez, Hume; passed on Bruno Fernandes at £12.0m with Mbeumo/Shaw/Lammens carrying the Man Utd run.

Held again with GW1 unfinished: no transfer, the free one banked to Friday, all three United men kept into Ipswich at home. Haaland (C) at Selhurst Park, B.Fernandes vice, 3-4-3 unchanged. Declined the Hull £4.0m defenders after their haul.

No move with Gameweek 1 one fixture from finished. Declined all three of the weekend's obvious buys — the Hull £4.0m defenders (all flagged at 75%), Sangaré's fourteen on debut, and Cherki's eight off the bench — on the grounds that a doubt or a substitute is not a seat. Graded Le Professeur's Gameweek 1 Bench Boost as spent rather than used at six points, while conceding he leads the five without it.

Settled Gameweek 1 at fifty points and fifth of eleven. Upgraded Palmer to nailed after thirteen on the opening night and named him, with Ødegaard, as the room's shape rather than its luck — neither is owned by any of the five. Sacked Palestra and Aït-Nouri as slots rather than players after both missed their clubs' matchday elevens, and sacked Cash and Watkins on Villa's week rather than on Villa's fixture. Recommended no transfer before Friday: every obvious buy is either one game old, flagged, or in the middle of a transfer.

No transfer recommended for the third run running, two days before the deadline and six before the window shuts — on the explicit grounds that an open window is a team-sheet risk rather than a shopping opportunity (D9). Downgraded Shaw on the reporting that United expect another left-back before Tuesday. Flipped the Gakpo case: the risk is no longer that Liverpool sell him but that they buy over him, with two bids rejected for one winger and two more targets live. Sacked Villa's goalkeeper as a slot, and Forest's incumbent striker on a £50m arrival. Corrected two errors of our own from Monday: The Special One's dead men were on his bench, not in his eleven, and Le Professeur's six-point Bench Boost is not a footnote to his lead, it is the whole of it.

Deadline eve, and no transfer recommended for the fifth run running — Friday’s deadline falls four days before the window shuts, so nothing bought now is bought with the team sheet known. Upgraded Woltemade on Osula’s knock and a cup start, and opened Barry at £5.5m on a hat-trick graded as a team sheet rather than a scoreline. Held Palestra at sack after Alonso said Chelsea "need to check a little bit more" ahead of a second missed fixture, and added the goalkeeper question alongside it. Cooled De Cuyper on Brighton’s injury list rather than on his seventeen points, and warned on Ajer as Brentford bought a fifth player and sold a centre-back. Sacked Baleba, Osula and Grealish as slots rather than players. Minted D10: a cup tie is a team sheet, not a fixture.

Deadline day. No transfer recommended for the sixth run running, on the grounds that the deadline falls four days before the window shuts and every squad in the room already has fifteen fit players. Settled two calls by transfer rather than by result: sacked Sánchez outright once Chelsea agreed £7.5m for Martinez, the exact trigger written on Monday, and killed the Gakpo case once Liverpool agreed £120m for Barcola — the trigger there was the window shutting with nobody arriving, and somebody arrived. Opened Martinez at £5.0m as a Tuesday buy rather than a Friday one, with Suzuki alongside him. Upgraded Woltemade to solid as Osula went from a 50% knock to no return date, and Konsa on the reporting that he starts at Villa Park. Downgraded Penders to sack behind the new goalkeeper. Cooled Guéhi on the grounds that his ten points came from central midfield, where a defender keeps no clean sheets. Opened Estêvão, James, Acheampong, Trafford, Tarkowski and Tonali. Minted D11: write triggers a transfer can settle, not only ones that need ninety minutes.

Saturday of a gameweek one fixture old. Upgraded Cherki to nailed on the start his trigger asked for, plus two goals at Selhurst Park, and recorded that not one of the five captained Haaland before he scored twice. Moved Guéhi back towards a buy once Maresca dropped the midfield experiment and played him at centre-back. Settled Watkins on the £50m Al-Hilal sale and Martinez on Villa confirming the Chelsea deal. Opened Foden, O'Reilly, Diouf, Delap and Muñoz. Recommended no transfer again, on the grounds that the window shuts on Tuesday and the GW3 deadline is the Friday after it — the first week of the season in which waiting costs nothing. Minted D12 on the armband.

Saturday's five fixtures settled four open triggers and opened a hole. Upgraded Tarkowski to solid on the late goal at Bournemouth, exactly the trigger written on Thursday. Sacked Tonali, whose trigger was ninety minutes against Newcastle and who was substituted in a 2-0 defeat, and sacked Gravenberch, who was left out of the pivot rather than keeping a clean sheet in it. Moved Igor Jesus back to watch after he started at Anfield ahead of the £45m Delap, and cooled Delap for the same reason. Cooled Kerkez after he was taken off on 71 minutes, and cooled Woltemade after Wissa scored at Spurs and Napoli were reported to want him on loan. Settled Sánchez and Muñoz by transfer. Opened Isak, Gibbs-White, Elanga, Wissa, Scott and the three Hull picks. Minted D13 against the brain's own D5: the £4.0m Hull defenders it declined after one haul now have two clean sheets behind them and thirty-six points between them. Recommended no transfer until the window shuts on Tuesday.

Gameweek 2 settled everything except Villa v Arsenal. Marked the brain's own Bench Boost rule under review after Sir Fergie played one in a single gameweek and won the week and the lead with it — D14. Upgraded B.Fernandes on a hat-trick that fired his blank trigger the other way, and upgraded Maguire, Lammens, Schade, Calvert-Lewin, Wissa, Ajayi and Tzolakis. Sacked Lacroix on the exact trigger written on Thursday — a clean sheet against a depleted Brighton — after Chelsea conceded three and reached eighteen games without one. Sacked Caicedo, who came off in tears after eleven minutes, Kerkez a week early on the substitution rather than the missed start, Welbeck on an unused bench at 4-3, and Woltemade once Wissa started and scored. Cooled Ndiaye with Spurs in advanced talks, Semenyo on one assist at £8.5m, De Cuyper on an advanced role that is not the position he was bought for, and Havertz on Arsenal chasing Álvarez. Opened Rashford, Neto and Groß. Recommended no transfer until the window shuts on Tuesday, with the deadline three days behind it.
